description: Approximate, faster center-star MSA: picks the center by 4-mer count cosine similarity, builds a suffix tree on it and aligns every other sequence with exact-match anchors (MUMmer-style seed, weighted colinear chain, Needleman–Wunsch — or Gotoh affine with gapModel='affine' — on the gaps between anchors). The pairwise alignments are NOT guaranteed optimal, so the sum-of-pairs score can be lower than multiple_align's. Default linear gap model (gapOpen ignored); gapModel='affine' charges gapOpen + k·gapExtend per gap run and reports the natural affine sum-of-pairs score. PROTEIN / MATRIX: type='protein' (or matrix) scores anchors as the sum of matrix(c, c) and fills the gaps between anchors with the matrix aligner (any alphabet); rows equal an independent Python implementation (anchors = suffix-tree matching statistics, colinear chain, Needleman-Wunsch / Gotoh between anchors).

sequences.description: Sequences to align (at least one): DNA (A, C, G, T) by default, amino acids with type='protein'.

gapOpen.description: Gap-open penalty. Used only with gapModel='affine' (a gap of length k then costs gapOpen + k * gapExtend, Gotoh); ignored by the default linear model. May be fractional only with a substitution matrix (type='protein' or matrix).

gapExtend.description: Gap penalty per gap position (linear model: every gap position; affine model: the per-position part of gapOpen + k * gapExtend). May be fractional (e.g. -0.5) only with a substitution matrix (type='protein' or matrix).

gapModel.description: 'linear' (default): every gap position costs gapExtend and gapOpen is ignored; totalScore is the column sum of pairs (gap-gap columns 0). 'affine': gap runs cost gapOpen + k * gapExtend; the pairwise / profile alignments use affine (Gotoh) dynamic programming and totalScore is the sum of pairs with natural affine gap costs (Altschul 1989: each pair of rows is projected out of the alignment, gap-gap columns skipped, every gap run of the projection pays gapOpen once). For two sequences the affine result is an optimal pairwise alignment; for three or more sequences every method is a heuristic.

type.description: Sequence type: 'dna' (default; A, C, G, T scored with match/mismatch) or 'protein' (amino-acid sequences scored with the substitution matrix, default BLOSUM62; match/mismatch are then ignored). The protein path shares the dynamic programs, merge, profile and objective code of the DNA path (no second implementation).

matrix.description: Optional substitution matrix: BLOSUM62 or PAM250 (type='protein'), EDNAFULL (IUPAC DNA, type='dna'). When given (or type='protein'), match/mismatch are ignored, residues are scored by the published table (case-insensitive, any symbol of the matrix), gapOpen/gapExtend may be fractional (EMBOSS needle numbers gapopen G / gapextend E = gapOpen -(G - E), gapExtend -E) and the result also carries the real-valued exactTotalScore (totalScore = rounded). Verified against independent Python implementations of every method, Biopython 1.88 pairwise optima and exhaustive enumeration of tiny sets.

alignedSequences.description: The aligned rows of the MSA.

consensus.description: Majority-vote consensus of the aligned rows (gaps vote; a nucleotide beats a gap on ties).

totalScore.description: Sum-of-pairs score of the MSA: linear model = column score (match/mismatch from the matrix, residue-gap = gapExtend, gap-gap = 0); gapModel='affine' = natural affine gap costs (every gap run of each pair projection pays gapOpen once).

exactTotalScore.description: Real-valued sum-of-pairs score (= totalScore for DNA with integer scores; the exact score, e.g. 49.5, for substitution-matrix runs with fractional gaps, where totalScore is rounded half away from zero).
